name: gemm
title: A streamed inference layer: read-only 16-bit weights from an external memory, activation vectors in, results out, exact arithmetic; throughput per area
_status: Stage 1 (2026-11-25): an exploration task. There is no trusted statement yet; entries are UNPROVED, checked by simulation against oracle.py (check/explore.py) and scored by composition (score/hier.py). Nothing of it is ranked with the proved records.
What a future statement will say is described in README.md ("What a proof will have to show").
_kind_comment: check.py's kind for a task without a statement: only `--unproved` runs, with the entry's declaration (`--declare`: the cycle formula and the memory layout). Clocked: the source gate's clocked rules apply (one clock, posedge, synchronous reset).
_range_comment: E = 2^LGE entries per stream beat (a beat is 16*E bits; 2048 bits at LGE = 7); LAT is the memory's burst latency. The layer size N is a run-time value, E <= N <= 32*E (128..4096 at LGE = 7), and so is the batch, 1..65535.
_clock_comment: One clock (rising edge) and a synchronous, active-high reset held at least one cycle. Every output is a register (Moore).

protocol._comment: README.md, "The interface": the job channel (the layer's size, batch and output-stage parameters), the memory request and data channels (sequential bursts, one at a time, first beat LAT cycles after the request), the activation channel, the result channel with its position tag. A transfer happens where valid and ready are both 1; a sender holds valid and payload until then.

banlist._comment: No task-specific banlist: * is the task's tool. Run-time / % ** are banned in every task.

scoring.label: composed
scoring._comment: The composed ASAP7 score (score/hier.py, cells only): area = sum over the distinct modules of instances x own cells, plus the SRAM catalogue blocks by table; period = the slowest module's own register-to-register period at these parameters (each module alone, its child instances cut at their pins; the hierarchy rule makes that meaningful); cycles = the entry's declared steady-state cycles per job at the scored job (N = 4096, batch 4096), a formula the simulations confirm at every simulated point and on the scored job itself (run twice with identity weights). Score = area x cycles x period, lower is better; shown as mm2*ms per job. No sky130 column: this task is scored on ASAP7.

explore._comment: The simulated points (check/explore.py): at each, `seeds` runs of a job list (`shapes`: [log2(N/E), batch] per job, or the word `sweep`: the oracle's 64 jobs, one per shift of the output stage; the seed picks the list) from a random power-up state under random pauses, each repeated on data of another kind (the schedule must not change), and the cycle check at `cycle_shapes` (four identical jobs back to back, nominal timing). At the point marked `netlist` the result runs are repeated on the gate netlist the pinned passes write with the hierarchy kept, as for the score. Batches above 2*E exercise more than one chunk of a design that buffers 2*E vectors. The last point is the SCORED parameters: the design text as it is scored, on its own job lists (`shapes`, `cycle_shapes`: N = 128 and 256 with a few vectors, and the largest layer, N = 4096, with one vector), and, marked `scored_job`, the scored job itself twice back to back at nominal timing with identity weights, whose measured cycles must equal the declared formula there (`mem_beats`, `x_beats`: the environment's memory depths, here and for every point; a declared layout stores more beats than the canonical one, and a job list that needs more than the depth is reported as the task's fault). It is marked `static: false`: the stages that flatten the design in Yosys (the banlist's backstop, the 4-state rules) run at the other points, which the rating build can flatten.

entries.note: par: the plain classical array (own code, generated by reference/gen.py). E x E multiply-accumulate cells, double-buffered weight tiles, an on-chip activation buffer of 2 E vectors, a two-block accumulator memory and an output stage per row.

fip: the inner-product form (own code, generated by reference/gen_fip.py). Half the multipliers per row on operands two bits wider; the weight term once per loaded tile row, the activation term once per slice. The rest is par's machine.

s1: one level of Strassen (the original form) on one shared array (own code, generated by reference/gen_strassen.py). Seven stored 17-bit weight combinations in a declared layout, activation sums formed from a four-bank buffer, each product added with its signs into the result blocks it feeds.

s2: two levels of Strassen on three arrays, one per class of leaf products, running the same schedule side by side (own code, generated by reference/gen_strassen.py). 49 stored 18-bit weight combinations.
s2s: two levels of Strassen on one shared array (own code, generated by reference/gen_strassen.py). 49 stored 18-bit weight combinations.

fip_sign: a player's entry, the files as submitted (no generator writes them). fip with the cell's signed 18 x 18 product written as one unsigned 18 x 18 product, two conditional sign rows and a corner term; the rest of the design and the declaration are fip's.
